text:
Tom Wilson's season took another turn today. He got a boarding major and a game misconduct at 8:55 of the first period for a hit that sent Florida's Sandis Vilmanis out of the game (ESPN, Daily Faceoff). Washington still won 4-3 without him. Whether the league adds a suspension is the open question, and it lands in the middle of a slump: Wilson now has no points in eleven straight games.

The slump is a mix of real and unlucky. He has two goals on five goals' worth of chances (expected goals measure the quality of his looks), and he keeps getting them, which is the part that usually turns. The Capitals still win the chance battle with him on (55.6% at 5v5). His line's chances have thinned a bit, though. Last season he scored 30, and NHL.com reported the GM calls re-signing him a "big priority." Evolving-Hockey rated him among the best defensive forwards in the league in 2025-26. Our projection still sees around 20 more goals this season. A suspension would push the turnaround further away.
headline: Tom Wilson's slump, and a hit that may cost more
